title: SAE Sparsity Comparison: Text-Only GPT-2 vs Multimodal CLIP Encoder on the Same Concept Set

original_idea.problem: SAEs trained on vision-language models like CLIP show different sparsity properties than those on pure language models. The causal mechanism is not understood.
original_idea.direction: Train matched SAEs on GPT-2-small's residual stream and CLIP's text encoder. Measure L0 sparsity, monosemanticity scores, and feature splitting rates. Vary training data distribution.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Plausible chain: understanding why vision pretraining changes feature geometry helps predict representation structure in frontier multimodal models. The safety relevance is indirect — it informs interpretability tool design for multimodal systems, but doesn't directly address a safety failure mode.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Training SAEs on two different model architectures, implementing matching configurations, and measuring monosemanticity scores requires significant ML and interpretability experience. Understanding SAE training dynamics and feature evaluation is beyond beginner level.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Two SAE training runs plus evaluation is conceptually bounded, but the 'vary training data distribution' extension opens scope. The core comparison (GPT-2 vs CLIP SAE metrics) is a clear first deliverable, but SAE training requires careful hyperparameter tuning.

novelty.reasoning: Multiple papers directly address SAE application to CLIP and vision-language models. 'Sparse Autoencoders Learn Monosemantic Features in Vision-Language Models' (NeurIPS 2025) systematically evaluates SAE sparsity and monosemanticity on CLIP. 'Interpreting CLIP with Hierarchical Sparse Autoencoders' (arXiv:2502.20578) introduces Matryoshka SAEs for CLIP. A Stanford CS231N report directly compares learned features in CLIP models via SAEs. 'Understanding and comparing learned features in CLIP models via Sparse Autoencoders' covers the cross-modal comparison. The proposed GPT-2 vs CLIP comparison adds incremental value but the core methodology and findings on CLIP SAE sparsity properties are well-established.
